wdVmNaN.purpose: Carry from iteration-5 NB-2: assert NaN contract on the strict VM because the interpreter's evaluator makes NaN >= x true (ailang#1419), so `ailang test` cannot see a NaN-guard defect
wdVmNaN.measured_correct: Interpreter 3000.0/3000.0/false; strict VM 3000.0/3000.0/false (verified independently by running $A run --quiet --package-dir sim --entry run on a scratch module that imports the published package)
killed_mutations: M-C: in bbTeffFromBpRpExact, drop the bpRp == bpRp guard. Interpreter: NaN >= bbBpRp(3000.0) is true (ailang#1419), first arm returns 3000.0 (masked bug). Strict VM: NaN >= x is false, bisect path; bbBpRp(exp(m)) > NaN is false on the VM so the recursion always takes the else arm, converges, returns 3000.0000000000136. The wd-vm gate (== 3000.0) catches this: 3000.0000000000136 != 3000.0 → wd-nan-BAD → make wd-vm fails. This is the exact value iteration 5 measured (3000.0000000000136).
wdVmNaN.scope_caveat: The wd-vm gate is load-bearing against NaN-comparison defects in bbTeffFromBpRpExact, where the NaN guard is the bpRp == bpRp short-circuit. A NaN-guard removal inside the lookup function in bbTeffFromBpRp is masked by the outer bbClampTeff (the value 2999.9999999999973 is < 3000.0, so the clamp returns 3000.0 and the == 3000.0 check still passes). Empirical confirmation: my scratch mutant `let cc = c; ...` in lookup_correct gave correct=3000.0 on both interpreter and VM after clamp; a similar mutation in the exact path gave 3000.0 on the interpreter and 3000.0000000000136 on the VM.

non_blocking.finding: design_docs/stapledon-mission-log.md was not appended to. The sprint plan task 6 says: 'append a mission-log note to design_docs/stapledon-mission-log.md (the renumbering is a planning detail recorded in the log, not the ledger).' git diff shows zero changes to that file. The renumbering is correctly recorded in the design doc itself (m1-relativistic-sky.md M1.3 and M1.2d sections, m1-relativistic-sky-sprint.md §M1.2d), so the user-facing facts are intact; the only missing artefact is the optional mission-log entry. Recommend appending it as a follow-up before the M1.2c sprint starts, so the WD-3 milestone has the same mission-log trail as WD-1/WD-2.

The wd-vm gate is the only test for bbTeffFromBpRpExact(NaN). The bbTeffFromBpRp path (the production inversion) is only covered by checkWDPackage on a non-NaN fixture. Iteration 5's M2 found that dropping the c == c guard in lookup is masked by the outer bbClampTeff on both engines; iteration 6's wd-vm is the right scope-creep response, but a second test that exercises bbTeffFromBpRp with a non-table colour that should clamp (e.g. -10 or 100) on the strict VM would tighten the load-bearing property. Not blocking — the existing wd-vm gate plus the AC-W5 parity check (full sim path through the WD module) already pin the production path.

make wd-vm trusts the literal string 'wd-nan-ok' from the wdVmNaN entry point. A test that always returns 'wd-nan-ok' would pass the gate (M4b). The recipe should be paired with a `git diff --exit-code` on sim/tools/catalogue_probe_test.ail to catch local tampering of the test, similar to how the deps recipe treats the lockfile. Not blocking for the present sprint because the test file is in scope for the M1.2c follow-up's bounded production tasks and any future edit would be visible in `git diff`.
